concept.title: Use cases for the Node Health Check Operator
concept.shortdesc: The Node Health Check Operator is a "Rolling Stream" Operator, meaning updates are available asynchronously of OpenShift Container Platform releases.

conbody.p: When unhealthy nodes are identified, the Node Health Check (NHC) Operator can be used with the other remediation providers, including:

note.p: Due to the existence of preinstalled machine health checks on Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA) clusters, the Node Health Check Operator is unable to function in such an environment.

conbody.p: The Node Health Check Operator detects the health of the nodes in a cluster. The NodeHealthCheck controller creates the NodeHealthCheck custom resource (CR), which defines a set of criteria and thresholds to determine the health of a node.

When the Node Health Check Operator detects an unhealthy node, it creates a remediation CR that triggers the remediation provider. For example, the controller creates the SelfNodeRemediation CR, which triggers the Self Node Remediation Operator to remediate the unhealthy node.
The NodeHealthCheck CR resembles the following YAML file, with self-node-remediation as the remediation provider:
conbody.codeblock: apiVersion: remediation.medik8s.io/v1alpha1 kind: NodeHealthCheck metadata: name: nodehealthcheck-sample spec: minHealthy: 51% maxUnhealthy: 29% pauseRequests: - <pause-test-cluster> stormCooldownDuration: 60s remediationTemplate: apiVersion: self-node-remediation.medik8s.io/v1alpha1 name: self-node-remediation-resource-deletion-template namespace: openshift-workload-availability kind: SelfNodeRemediationTemplate escalatingRemediations: - remediationTemplate: apiVersion: self-node-remediation.medik8s.io/v1alpha1 name: self-node-remediation-resource-deletion-template namespace: openshift-workload-availability kind: SelfNodeRemediationTemplate order: 1 timeout: 300s selector: matchExpressions: - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/worker operator: Exists unhealthyConditions: - type: Ready status: "False" duration: 300s - type: Ready status: Unknown duration: 300s

ul.li: minHealthy: Specifies the amount of healthy nodes (in percentage or number) required for a remediation provider to concurrently remediate nodes in the targeted pool. If the number of healthy nodes equals to or exceeds the limit set by minHealthy, remediation occurs. The default value is 51%.

maxUnhealthy: Specifies the amount of unhealthy nodes (in percentage or number) permitted for a remediation provider to concurrently remediate nodes in the targeted pool. If the number of unhealthy nodes exceeds the limit set by maxUnhealthy, no further remediation occurs. There is no default value. The usage of maxUnhealthy is mutually exclusive to the usage of minHealthy.

pauseRequests: Prevents any new remediation from starting, while allowing any ongoing remediations to persist. The default value is empty. However, you can enter an array of strings that identify the cause of pausing the remediation. For example, pause-test-cluster.
During the upgrade process, nodes in the cluster might become temporarily unavailable and get identified as unhealthy. In the case of worker nodes, when the Operator detects that the cluster is upgrading, it stops remediating new unhealthy nodes to prevent such nodes from rebooting.

stormCooldownDuration: Specifies the timeout duration of the stabilization phase that occurs immediately after a "storm". A storm happens when the number of healthy or unhealthy nodes exceeds the threshold values defined by minHealthy or maxUnhealthy. Remediation creation is blocked during the active storm, remains blocked for this additional cooldown duration, and until the threshold values are satisfied again. This cooldown duration ensures that nodes recovering from a mass failure have sufficient time to report their status before normal remediation logic resumes.

remediationTemplate: Specifies a remediation template from the remediation provider. For example, from the Self Node Remediation Operator. remediationTemplate is mutually exclusive with escalatingRemediations.

escalatingRemediations: Specifies a list of RemediationTemplates with order and timeout fields. To obtain a healthy node, use this field to sequence and configure multiple remediations. This strategy increases the likelihood of obtaining a healthy node, instead of depending on a single remediation that might not be successful. The order field determines the order in which the remediations are invoked (lower order = earlier invocation). The timeout field determines when the next remediation is invoked. escalatingRemediations is mutually exclusive with remediationTemplate.
When escalatingRemediations is used the remediation providers, Self Node Remediation Operator and Fence Agents Remediation Operator, can be used multiple times with different remediationTemplate configurations. However, you can not use the same Machine Deletion Remediation configuration with different remediationTemplate configurations.
selector: Specifies a selector that matches labels or expressions that you want to check. Avoid selecting both control-plane and worker nodes in one CR.
unhealthyConditions: Specifies a list of the conditions that determine whether a node is considered unhealthy.

duration: Specifies the timeout duration for a node condition. If a condition is met for the duration of the timeout, the node will be remediated. Long timeouts can result in long periods of downtime for a workload on an unhealthy node.

conbody.p: The NodeHealthCheck CR resembles the following YAML file, with metal3 as the remediation provider:
conbody.codeblock: apiVersion: remediation.medik8s.io/v1alpha1 kind: NodeHealthCheck metadata: name: nhc-worker-metal3 spec: minHealthy: 30% remediationTemplate: apiVersion: infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1 kind: Metal3RemediationTemplate name: metal3-remediation namespace: openshift-machine-api selector: matchExpressions: - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/worker operator: Exists unhealthyConditions: - duration: 300s status: 'False' type: Ready - duration: 300s status: 'Unknown' type: Ready

note.p: The matchExpressions are examples only; you must map your machine groups based on your specific needs.

conbody.p: The Metal3RemediationTemplate resembles the following YAML file, with metal3 as the remediation provider:
conbody.codeblock: apiVersion: infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1 kind: Metal3RemediationTemplate metadata: name: metal3-remediation namespace: openshift-machine-api spec: template: spec: strategy: retryLimit: 1 timeout: 5m0s type: Reboot

note.p: In addition to creating a NodeHealthCheck CR, you must also create the Metal3RemediationTemplate.
